Hi Mina / Marissa,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. A couple of items procurement needs to confirm before we move to SOW:

- How does Redwood meter very long transcript ingests? We have archival transcripts that can be 200k+ tokens; are those charged differently (e.g., 'context ingests' vs API calls)?
- Rounding and minimums: is there a per-request minimum or per-session floor? How do you round partial-token usage (up, down, nearest)?
- If we enable streaming and long-lived sessions with KV cache reuse, do we still hit the same minimums (e.g., every stream counted as a call)?
- If Redwood automatically falls back to a quantized model when capacity is constrained, does that trigger a different billing rate or a credit if the result quality degrades?

Attached: Beacon_SOW_v1.pdf (SOW draft) — we included estimated monthly token volumes. Also attaching some sample transcripts separately.

Procurement will need clear sample invoices or arithmetic we can pass to our finance team. Can you provide sample line-items for three scenarios: low-volume pilot (50k tokens/month), steady state (2M tokens/month), and batch archival loads (5-10M tokens/month occasional spikes)?

Appreciate a concise breakdown and any contract language you recommend for minimums / degradation credits.

Hi — thanks for the clear list. TL;DR up top, then examples and contract language suggestions below.

TL;DR
- We bill per-token (input + output) with sub-token precision internally but invoice at token granularity. For commercial invoices we round to the nearest 10-token bucket for efficiency; pilot invoices can be exact on request.
- There is a per-request floor only for very short calls; for streaming / long sessions we apply a per-session floor of 100 tokens, which is then aggregated per billing window for customers without committed minimums.
- KV/prefix reuse reduces billable tokens because repeated context is cached — we do not charge again for cache hits within a session.
- If we fail over to a lower-precision/quantized model for capacity reasons we do not change the nominal price per token; instead we offer a "quality degradation credit" while we investigate. We typically propose 20% credit (capped) for measurable regressions tied to a defined prompt set.

Examples (invoice-oriented):
1) Low-volume pilot — 50k tokens/month (mixed ingest + generation)
   - Raw tokens: 50,412 -> rounded to 50,410 (nearest 10 tokens)
   - Metered charges: 50,410 tokens * $0.0008 = $40.33
   - Per-session floors applied? negligible at this scale (few sessions >100 tokens)

2) Steady state — 2,000,000 tokens/month
   - Raw tokens: 2,002,378 -> rounded to 2,002,380
   - Metered charges: 2,002,380 * $0.0007 (volume price) = $1,401.67
   - Example: KV cache saved ~18% of tokens on repeat prefixes (line-item: cache-savings credit shown as informational, not deducted unless agreed)

3) Batch archival loads (spike) — 10,000,000 tokens in a day
   - Batched ingestion is treated as standard token billing; we recommend sending large archival uploads as a single batch window to avoid per-request floors.
   - Raw tokens: 10,015,122 -> rounded to 10,015,120
   - Metered charges: 10,015,120 * $0.0006 (spike tier) = $6,009.07

Notes on rounding/minimums
- Default rounding: nearest 10-token bucket on invoices; internal metering is more precise for debugging.
- Per-session floor: 100 tokens per session for streaming/long sessions (to account for warmup). If you enable committed capacity / Dedicated we can waive per-session floors.
- Short-call floor: calls under 10 tokens are rounded up to 10 tokens.

Quality fallback / degradation credits (contract language suggestion)
- "If Redwood automatically serves a compatible, lower-precision model (e.g., 8-bit quantized variant) due to capacity constraints, Redwood will notify Beacon Health and provide a measurable evaluation on a mutually agreed prompt set. If the delivered outputs fall below agreed quality thresholds, Beacon Health will receive a credit equal to 20% of billed tokens for the affected billing period, capped at $25,000 per incident, unless otherwise agreed in writing."

Attachments: I exported a quick token_usage_sample.csv that shows the rounding and an example invoice layout.

If that looks good I can loop in Karthik to finalize the commercial concession (pilot/discount language) and pass an SOW clean copy for signatures. Do you want the pilot to be no-minimum for the first 60 days?

Internal notes for negotiation (do not forward without sign-off):

- Proposal: 60-day pilot with no minimum and invoice rounding at nearest 10 tokens. Offer a temporary 8% volume discount for first 3 months if they commit to >500k tokens/month after pilot. Rationale: removes procurement friction and buys time to tune KV caching for Beacon workloads.
- Degradation credit: make it explicit and narrow. Suggest: 20% credit on affected billed tokens with a diagnostics window. Suggest: Add an SLA clause that requires Beacon to provide failing prompt set within 10 business days and Redwood to respond within 5 business days with mitigation plan. Cap credit at lesser of $25k or one monthly invoice.
- Context-shedding / prefix handoff: define expected behavior in SOW: when context > model limit, we will (a) preserve prefix tokens marked as sticky, (b) shed oldest non-sticky tokens, (c) offer a post-ingest report showing any dropped tokens and the timestamp. Billing-wise, shed tokens are not billable if explicitly dropped during ingestion pipeline; if you request a reingest later, that is billable at the then-applicable rate.

Marissa — can you draft the short SOW paragraph for prefix shedding + degradation credit with the 10-day diagnostic requirement? I'll prepare the concession approval for legal.

Karthik
Director, Commercials | Redwood Inference

Thanks — that level of detail is helpful. We are happy to proceed with:

- 60-day pilot, no minimum; Redwood to provide invoice examples for pilot period showing exact token math.
- If post-pilot Beacon commits to >=500k tokens/month for 3 months, Redwood will apply an 8% volume credit for those 3 months.
- Degradation credit clause as proposed (20% credit, capped, with 10-day diagnostic window) — acceptable to legal with minor wording tweaks.
- Prefix shedding behavior OK; please include the "post-ingest report" language and the non-billable handling for dropped tokens in the SOW.
